newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 13.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* Hicks Muse agreed to buy LIN Television for $1.4 billion, or $47.50 a share, as well as the 46 percent of LIN owned by AT&T.
* Stocks tumbled Tuesday on fears that today's reports on retail sales and producer prices will show a jump in inflation.
* The AFL-CIO authorized United Parcel Service's Teamsters union to borrow millions of dollars from it to help pay strike benefits.
* Columbia/HCA has been declared a target of the criminal investigation into whether the company defrauded the federal government.
* General Dynamics bid about $1.0 billion for military-vehicle maker United Defense in United's recent auction.
* Productivity rose 0.6 percent in the second-quarter, while labor costs rose 2.4 percent.
* The FCC is preparing to reject Ameritech's application to offer long-distance service in Michigan.
* ABC TV said the network is leaning toward using the government's digital spectrum rather than high-definition TV to broadcast several new channels.
* President Clinton is expected to nominate Treasury official Mozelle Thompson to fill a vacant seat at the FTC.
* Southeast Asian currencies fell further on Tuesday.
* Wal-Mart and TJX recorded strong second-quarter earnings, although J.C. Penney's earnings fell.
* Fidelity's mutual funds are staging a comeback after three medicore years for some of the company's biggest funds.
* A New York Stock Exchange advisory panel is proposing that the exchange ease Rule 500, which makes it hard for companies to leave the exchange.
* Gold stocks are rallying amid mounting investor worry about the future of the broader market.
* Bond prices fell moderately on worries that consumer spending is continuing to rise.
